blocked106.flaw_semantics: Mode-switch logic flaw in PX4 commander: while ARMED after landing (before COM_DISARM_LAND auto-disarm), switching Auto->Manual via RC/MAVLink is permitted with no physical throttle-stick threshold check, so a high-throttle stick position transfers directly to control allocation and causes rapid uncontrolled ascent/flyaway. The throttle thresholds _is_throttle_above_center/_is_throttle_low are computed (Commander.cpp:2961-2962) and enforced only in arm() denial gates (Commander.cpp:610-630), never on the armed mode-switch path: handle_command() DO_SET_MODE/SET_NAV_STATE (Commander.cpp:844-960) routes through UserModeIntention::change() (UserModeIntention.cpp:49-53) which while armed only checks _health_and_arming_checks.canRun(), not throttle position.
defect_lines: src/modules/commander/UserModeIntention.cpp:49-53 (change(): armed mode switch gated only by canRun(), no throttle check)
src/modules/commander/Commander.cpp:844-960 (handle_command DO_SET_MODE/SET_NAV_STATE: armed Auto->Manual switch without throttle-stick threshold)
src/modules/commander/Commander.cpp:2961-2962 (_is_throttle_above_center/_is_throttle_low computed but only used in arm() denial)

introducer.subject: commander arming: throttle above center / high throttle denial in arm()

blocked106.reasoning: The flaw is a missing safety check (design gap) in human-authored PX4 commander code, consolidated in Beat Küng's 2022 failsafe-state-machine refactor; the throttle-threshold enforcement exists only in the arm() path (Daniel Agar/Matthias Grob, 2021-2022), never in the armed mode-switch path. blocked106.flaw_semantics: listFFmpegProcesses() in plugin/API/standAlone/functions.php builds a shell command as ps ... | grep '[f]fmpeg' and, when a keyword is supplied, appends | grep '$keyword' with the keyword interpolated inside single quotes without escaping. partial_wave.bug_semantics: HMACAlgorithm.prepare_key accepted a raw JSON JWK document as an HMAC secret (only PEM/SSH formats were rejected), so a verifier configured with mixed algorithm families (e.g. HS256+RS256) and a raw-JSON JWK key could be tricked into verifying attacker-forged HS256 tokens signed with the issuer's public key (algorithm confusion, GHSA-xgmm-8j9v-c9wx). Fix in 2.13.0 rejects JWK JSON dicts as HMAC secrets and binds header alg to PyJWK.algorithm_name during verification.
partial_wave.flaw_origin: HMACAlgorithm.prepare_key was written to accept arbitrary bytes as the secret with only PEM/SSH guards; the JWK-JSON-as-HMAC-secret acceptance path existed since the algorithm class was created.

blocked106.flaw_semantics: FreeRDP audin (audio input redirection) client channel: server-supplied FramesPerPacket from the OPEN PDU is stored unvalidated (audin->FramesPerPacket = FramesPerPacket) and later used in buffer-size calculations by client backends (ALSA, sndio, WinMM, OpenSL ES) and freerdp_dsp_context_reset. legacy87.bug_semantics: mruby pattern matching compiler JMPNOT-to-JMPIF optimization unconditionally rewrote s->iseq[fail_pos - 2] = OP_JMPIF. When a pinned variable was undefined, NODE_PAT_PIN emitted a 3-byte OP_JMP rather than a 4-byte OP_JMPNOT, causing fail_pos - 2 to point into the prior instruction and corrupt bytecode operands, leading to VM crash/UAF. Sink: mrbgems/mruby-compiler/core/codegen.c:6408 (s->iseq[fail_pos - 2] = OP_JMPIF).
legacy87.flaw_origin: Commit 2b72d8a7c153e2afb22245ad9e40e0c7d5b1aa70 (Yukihiro Matz Matsumoto + Claude, 2025-12-23, Co-authored-by: Claude) introduced the JMPNOT-to-JMPIF optimization with s->iseq[fail_pos - 2] = OP_JMPIF without verifying the opcode; commit 1de6340f1bc81564274890660f66444e48d660b0 (also Claude co-authored) added the 3-byte OP_JMP path for undefined pinned variables.
legacy87.ai_role: 直接写了缺陷行
legacy87.adjudication_note: Claude co-authored commit 2b72d8a7 added the optimization rewriting fail_pos - 2 to OP_JMPIF without checking if the opcode was OP_JMPNOT. Combined with the pinned variable OP_JMP generation (also Claude co-authored in 1de6340f), this corrupted bytecode. Fix e50f15c1c6e131fa7934355eb02b8173b13df415 added the check s->iseq[fail_pos - 2] == OP_JMPNOT.

partial_wave.bug_semantics: SSH identification parsing accepted non-canonical client banners and did not bound pre-banner input (GHSA-76r6-x97p-67vr / CVE-2026-48108): russh/src/ssh_read.rs read_ssh_id() used one permissive path for both client and server - lines not starting with SSH- are treated as 'preliminary' pre-banner text and discarded in an unbounded loop (`ssh_id.total = 0; ssh_id.bytes_read = 0`), no line-count cap and no distinction that RFC 4253 section 4.2 only allows pre-banner lines from server to client. partial_wave.bug_semantics: Heap buffer over-read (1 byte) in the IPTC encoder path of coders/meta.c: while parsing an IPTC stream, the length-decoding loop reads c=(*p++) and accumulates tag_length; the guard 'if (tag_length > (length+1)) break' uses (length+1) instead of length, so a tag_length equal to length+1 passes the check and the subsequent p+=tag_length / length-=tag_length leaves length underflowed, letting the next iteration read past the buffer end when the malicious input supplies a crafted IPTC block. partial_wave.bug_semantics: CoreDNS transports (gRPC, QUIC, DoH, DoH3) failed to perform full TSIG cryptographic HMAC verification with dns.TsigVerify. On gRPC and QUIC, handlers only checked whether the TSIG key name existed in configuration and left tsigStatus as nil (verified); on DoH and DoH3, response writers unconditionally returned nil from TsigStatus(). This allowed unauthenticated attackers to forge TSIG records and bypass TSIG access controls (e.g. AXFR/IXFR transfers).

partial_wave.evidence: Fix commits 4c9a80c29 (PR #8006), 0e1870d76 (PR #8007), c0e6e7cef (PR #8013), and cf6a78f64 (PR #8044) by Yong Tang add full dns.TsigVerify verification across all four transports. Git blame shows transport response writer methods and initial key checks were written by human maintainer Yong Tang and earlier CoreDNS human contributors, with no AI markers.
partial_wave.reasoning: The incomplete TSIG verification logic across gRPC, QUIC, DoH, and DoH3 was implemented and maintained by human CoreDNS maintainers. There are no AI markers.

blocked106.flaw_semantics: Stored XSS: acqui/invoice-files.pl download handler serves invoice attachments inline (no Content-Disposition attachment) whenever request has view=1 and the stored file_type (client-supplied Content-Type captured at upload, untrusted) matches ^image/ or filename ends .pdf. An uploaded SVG (Content-Type image/svg+xml) with onload/script payload is therefore rendered inline by the browser on click, executing JS in the intranet session. Upload path (cud-upload) stores the browser-supplied Content-Type verbatim with no validation, so image/svg+xml passes through unchanged.

partial_wave.bug_semantics: TOCTOU symlink race bypass of domain=path policy (CWE-59): IsRightsAuthorized(PathPolicyDomain,...) is evaluated on the pathname before the file is opened/used (e.g. OpenBlob/FileToBlob/FileToImage in MagickCore/blob.c); an attacker who can swap the path to a symlink between check-time and open-time makes the policy check pass on an allowed path while the subsequent fopen_utf8/open_utf8 follows the symlink to a policy-denied file, bypassing read/write restrictions.
partial_wave.flaw_origin: 3ed852eea5 (cristy, 2009-09-05, Mercurial-era import snapshot): blame at 753ffb6999^ boundaries at 3ed852eea5 for the check-then-open pattern (IsRightsAuthorized(PathPolicyDomain,rights,filename) immediately followed by fopen_utf8/open_utf8 in OpenBlob, MagickCore/blob.c:3337-3340); design predates the git history available in this clone.
partial_wave.evidence: Advisory GHSA-493f-jh8w-qhx3 (CVE-2026-28689, published 2026-03-10): 'domain=path authorization is checked before final file open/use. A symlink swap between check-time and use-time bypasses policy-denied read/write.' Real fix: 753ffb6999 (Cristy 2026-02-22, message = GHSA URL): OpenBlob/FileToBlob/FileToImage now open with O_NOFOLLOW when system policy denies 'follow', and re-check IsRightsAuthorized(PathPolicyDomain,...) after opening (post-open re-check on the opened fd's path), closing the race; preceded by partial patch 3eb11260cf (2026-02-20) which Dirk Lemstra reverted in 818ee63632 (2026-02-22, 'committed by accident'); 753ffb6999 is a descendant of that revert and contains the full O_NOFOLLOW/post-open logic. Fix is ancestor of 7.1.2-18 (2026-03-xx), matching Magick.NET 14.10.4 fixed_version. Flaw origin: blame of the pre-fix OpenBlob shows the IsRightsAuthorized(PathPolicyDomain,...) check at 3ed852eea5 (2009), i.e. the check-then-use design is as old as the path policy itself. No AI markers on introducer/fix commits.
partial_wave.reasoning: The TOCTOU check-then-open pattern originates from cristy's 2009-era implementation (oldest reachable snapshot), and the fix was authored by the same maintainer in 2026 with a follow-up by Dirk Lemstra. No claude/copilot/gpt/co-authored/Codex markers anywhere in the chain -> NOT_AI

partial_wave.bug_semantics: Heap-buffer-overflow read (CWE-122) in MNG magnification: ReadOneJNGImage loads a separate alpha channel lazily - image->alpha_trait is flipped to BlendPixelTrait inside the pixel loop only when a non-opaque alpha is seen; if the first non-opaque pixel appears after GetAuthenticPixels has already been called for a row, the channel map is reset by the next GetAuthenticPixels (adding the alpha channel), so in the MAGN magnification path of ReadOneMNGImage the next/prev row buffers were sized from GetPixelChannels(image) BEFORE the alpha channel existed while the copy loop later reads them with GetPixelXXX assuming the enlarged layout, reading past the 1536-byte allocation (ASan: GetPixelRed at pixel-accessor.h:405, png.c:6657).
partial_wave.flaw_origin: 0208393691 (Dirk Lemstra, 2017-09-17, 'Some minor refactoring') restructured the alpha-copy loop into the if(alpha_trait!=Undefined) else branches and placed image->alpha_trait=BlendPixelTrait inside the else branch (lazy flip mid-loop); later d033472aa4 (Dirk Lemstra 2022-07-24) kept the lazy pattern while switching to a local alpha variable.
partial_wave.evidence: Advisory GHSA-cjc8-g9w8-chfw (CVE-2025-55004, published 2025-08-25, reporter: Google Big Sleep, reproduces on 7.1.2-0) describes the alpha_trait desync and the MAGN next/prev buffer under-allocation. Real fix: 55d97055e0 (Cristy 2025-08-07, message = GHSA URL): sets image->alpha_trait=BlendPixelTrait unconditionally before the pixel loop in ReadOneJNGImage, so the alpha channel is always in the channel map when buffers are sized (10 insertions, 23 deletions in coders/png.c). Fix is ancestor of 7.1.2-5 (2025-08-09), matching Magick.NET 14.8.0 fixed_version. Flaw origin: blame at 55d97055e0^ lines 4801-4821: the if/else alpha branch structure and the lazy 'image->alpha_trait=BlendPixelTrait' line originate at 0208393691 (Dirk Lemstra 2017-09-17); the local-alpha detection at d033472aa4 (Dirk Lemstra 2022). No AI markers on introducer or fix commits.
partial_wave.reasoning: The flaw (lazy mid-loop alpha_trait flip causing channel-map desync) was introduced by human Dirk Lemstra in 2017 and fixed by human Cristy in 2025. The AI in the loop was the reporter (Google Big Sleep fuzzer), not the code author; no AI authorship markers on the flaw line or the fix -> NOT_AI

partial_wave.bug_semantics: CWE-122 heap buffer over-write on 32-bit systems in the SFW decoder (coders/sfw.c ReadSFWImage): the overflow guard 'GetBlobSize(image) != (size_t) GetBlobSize(image)' is a tautology (size_t cast of a size_t value always compares equal), so for a huge SFW blob the subsequent AcquireQuantumMemory((size_t)GetBlobSize(image)+MagickPathExtent,...) wraps on 32-bit to a tiny allocation while ReadBlob then fills the full reported size, over-writing the heap. CVE-2026-31853 / GHSA-56jp-jfqg-f8f4.
partial_wave.flaw_origin: The ineffective no-op overflow check was added by 16881e68c6165c6191fc44151a8a4320e3dd1ffd (cristy 2012-05-06) in coders/sfw.c; the MagickPathExtent-padded allocation it was meant to guard came from d4145e664a (Cristy 2017-08-18).

Fix 7936d9c7bec4bd459a8d4b5304a1a6fbf7dac0ea (Dirk Lemstra 2026-03-02, 'Corrected the overflow check that can cause issues on 32-bit systems') computes extent=(size_t)GetBlobSize(image)+MagickPathExtent first and compares GetBlobSize(image) != extent to catch 32-bit wraparound, reusing extent for the allocation; first contained in tag 7.1.2-16 (7.1.2-15 affected). partial_wave.bug_semantics: Race condition in the distributed pixel cache server (MagickCore/distribute-cache.c) enabling file descriptor hijacking (CWE-362): the accept loop passes (void *) &client_socket, a stack variable reused on every iteration, to the spawned DistributePixelCacheClient thread; a fast second connection overwrites client_socket while the first thread is still using it, so the thread sends/reads on an fd it no longer owns and an attacker who can connect to the -distribute-cache service can hijack a file descriptor in the server process.
partial_wave.flaw_origin: The threaded accept loop was written passing a pointer to the stack-local client_socket into the client thread with no per-connection copy and no detached lifetime; the 2026 fix heap-allocates a per-connection socket slot that the thread consumes and frees, and detaches the threads.
partial_wave.evidence: GHSA-4g75-9r48-jf92 / CVE-2026-46693 (2026-05, Magick.NET, fixed 14.12.0): race condition in distributed pixel cache server can result in file descriptor hijacking. Fix 99711276a (2026-05-14, Cristy, message = advisory URL; preceded by adb4b8d7e removing an overflow check and d954e9c48 restoring it) rewrites the accept loop: client_socket_ptr=AcquireMagickMemory(sizeof(SOCKET_TYPE)); *client_socket_ptr=accept(...); the thread copies the value then RelinquishMagickMemory(ptr), and pthread_attr_setdetachstate(PTHREAD_CREATE_DETACHED) is added (MagickCore/distribute-cache.c:838-1075). git log -S pthread_create shows the racy pattern pthread_create(&threads,&attributes,DistributePixelCacheClient,(void *) &client_socket) was introduced by bb31fcd2d (2013-01-15, cristy, human) which rewrote distribute-cache.c into its threaded-server form. No AI markers.
partial_wave.reasoning: The shared-stack-socket threading race was written by human maintainer cristy in 2013. NOT_AI.

partial_wave.bug_semantics: In WSSecurityOneDotZeroReceiveSecurityHeader.VerifySignatureAsync, endorsing and supporting signature verification validated that the ds:Signature was structurally sound and verified its SignedInfo digests, but failed to enforce that the signature actually covered the expected target (the wsu:Timestamp on transport-security paths or the primary signature ID). partial_wave.bug_semantics: p2p message DoS with high memory usage (GHSA-689v-6xwf-5jf3 / CVE-2026-26313, details embargoed): eth/snap response handlers decoded inbound packets eagerly - eth/protocols/eth/handlers.go handleBlockBodies (pre-fix) does `res := new(BlockBodiesPacket); msg.Decode(res)` and even computes DeriveSha over every tx/uncle/withdrawal in the metadata closure BEFORE the response is matched against an active request and its size limits (dispatchResponse). A malicious peer can send a specially-crafted large response (within maxMessageSize) with an arbitrary request id, forcing full decode + hashing allocations - high memory usage per connection. Fix 0cba803fb (#33835, Felix Lange 2026-02-15) delays decoding via rlp.RawList until the response is confirmed to match an active request and not exceed its limits (per-peer Tracker); block-body decoding delayed until after response-hash verification

去引号还原原始参数 → 重引号检测到 $VAR 模式改套双引号 → 反引号 payload 在双引号内执行。仅需 --allow-run（CWE-78 命令注入），
影响 v2.7.0/v2.7.1

partial_wave.bug_semantics: MCP server config security bypass enabling RCE: (1) docker build/compose not on the flag blocklist lets a low-privilege chatflow editor pull and execute a remote Dockerfile; (2) npx --yes long alias bypasses the -y blocklist to auto-install+run a malicious npm package; (3) regex /^\/[^/]/ in validateArgsForLocalFileAccess misses //-prefixed absolute paths, letting node run local files -> arbitrary command execution on the server.

partial_wave.evidence: GHSA-m99r-2hxc-cp3q documents all three bypasses against packages/components/nodes/tools/MCP/core.ts (validateCommandFlags blocklist missing docker build/compose, npx --yes, node require/loader flags; regex /^\/[^/]/ failing on //paths). Fix 7176dcb40 (#5943, 2026-03-23, christopherholland-workday) adds build/compose/mount/device/entrypoint to docker, --yes/--node-options to npx, -r/--require/--loader/--experimental-loader/--import/--env-file to node, and changes the regex to /^\//. git show flowise@3.1.1:.../MCP/core.ts confirms the vulnerable validation functions existed in 3.1.1; they were created by b4665df8d (#5741, 2026-02-24, christopherholland-workday, human, no AI marker) - before that commit no validateCommandFlags/validateArgsForLocalFileAccess existed (prior validation was CUSTOM_MCP_SECURITY_CHECK env gates from 41131dfac #5232, Henry Heng). Fix 7176dcb40 has no AI co-author either.
partial_wave.reasoning: The defective security checks (incomplete blocklist + flawed regex) were authored by a human in the commit that introduced MCP command validation; the AI marker rule finds no AI authorship on introducer or fix. NOT_AI.

partial_wave.bug_semantics: GHSA-4xjf-493q-98p3 (CVE-2026-56657): SSH key ingestion (POST /api/v1/user/keys, also web form) accepts RFC 4716 (SSH2) format; parseKeyString in models/asymkey/ssh_key_parse.go splits on newlines and accumulates with 'keyContent += line' (immutable Go string concat => O(N^2) time+allocations) with no input size limit, so a ~38MB key of 400k short lines forces quadratic CPU/memory work before any validity check; any authenticated user can exhaust the server.

partial_wave.bug_semantics: AppSec silently drops the request body for chunked / HTTP-2 requests (CVE-2026-44982, GHSA-rw47-hm26-6wr7): NewParsedRequestFromRequest in pkg/appsec/request.go computed contentLength := max(r.ContentLength, 0) and did body := make([]byte, contentLength); io.ReadFull(r.Body, body), so requests with ContentLength == -1 (chunked or HTTP/2 without known length) allocate a 0-byte body and skip reading, silently emptying the body and bypassing WAF body rules.

squash_audit.bug_semantics: 远程 $ref schema 获取未校验私有/本地 IP 地址导致服务端请求伪造（CWE-918 SSRF）。http.py 中 get_body() 使用 httpx.get(url) 获取远程 schema 内容，默认未限制目标 IP，攻击者可通过 schema 中的 $ref 指向内网敏感服务（如云元数据 169.254.169.254 或 localhost）窃取敏感信息或探测内网。sink=httpx.get(url)，source=JSON Schema 中的远程 $ref URL，guard=缺少针对本地与私有 IP 地址的 _validate_url_for_fetch 与 _is_safe_ip 校验。
squash_audit.flaw_origin: NOT_AI: http.py 中使用 httpx.get 获取远程 URL 且无私有 IP 限制的基础实现由人类维护者 Koudai Aono 于 2021 年在 commit 5609aa5bd79a 首次引入；候选 f6d4cbd3440a (PR #3051, Mikhail Butvin + Claude Opus 4.6) 旨在新增 --allow-remote-refs 闸门和 HTTP 错误包装，未编写导致 SSRF 的核心网络拉取与无 IP 校验逻辑
squash_audit.ai_marker: Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) on candidate f6d4cbd3440a (which only added --allow-remote-refs gate and error wrappers, not the SSRF sink)
squash_audit.evidence: git log -S 'def get_body' 确认 http.py 的网络请求功能由 Koudai Aono 在 2021-03-06 (commit 5609aa5bd79a, human) 首次实现。候选 f6d4cbd3440a (PR #3051, Mikhail Butvin) 在 http.py 中仅增加了 SchemaFetchError 包装和 Content-Type/status_code 校验，并新增 --allow-remote-refs 参数，未引入无 IP 校验的 SSRF 漏洞。Fix 5fdba4a09f2d (Koudai Aono, 2026-06-09) 新增 _validate_url_for_fetch, _is_safe_ip, _get_ips_from_host 等 100+ 行完整的私有 IP 拦截防护。

partial_wave.bug_semantics: docker cp into a container: daemon builds a temporary container FS view by bind-mounting volumes; mount destination path is resolved with GetResourcePath then passed to fileutils.CreateIfNotExists (os.Stat/os.MkdirAll/os.OpenFile on the host-absolute path). Introducer 2bdc7fb0a1e00439aa88438f1164677dda95737f (Cory Snider 2022-10-12, 'daemon: archive in a dedicated mount namespace') created containerfs_linux.go with the GetResourcePath + fileutils.CreateIfNotExists(dest, ...) pattern (lines 84/94 of the added file). partial_wave.bug_semantics: CVE-2026-49262 / GHSA-mmj8-wcvw-6789: SSRF via DNS rebinding (TOCTOU, CWE-367/918) in the admin cmsproxy route. partial_wave.flaw_origin: Commit a647b6cd (2025-07-01) rewrote the proxy fetch to remove the IP pinning that the original proxy controller (d8d80e4e, 2025-06-30) had: it dropped ->baseUrl("://") (host resolved once, then connected directly to that IP, immune to rebinding) and replaced it with ->send(, ) which re-resolves DNS at request time, creating the check-then-fetch TOCTOU window.

partial_wave.evidence: admin/src/Controllers/AdminController.php proxy(): in 0.10.3 the fetch used ->fetch(, , ) after Utils::isValidUrl() (core/src/Utils.php:217-222); introduced by a647b6cd (Aimeos <aimeos@aimeos.org>, 2025-07-01) which removed ->baseUrl("://") from the original d8d80e4e implementation; fixed by 09a8205 (Aimeos, 2025-05-25) which resolves the host once via Utils::resolve() and pins it with CURLOPT_RESOLVE (host:port:ip). squash_audit.bug_semantics: NodeVM 的 nesting 守卫不完整：候选 46cbbdde（修 GHSA-8hg8）在构造函数写入 if (options.nesting === true && options.require === false) throw，但 destructuring 默认值 require: requireOpts = false 使 require 省略/undefined/null/0/'' 全部塌缩为同一 NESTING_OVERRIDE-only resolver（makeResolverFromLegacyOptions 的 if (!options) 分支，唯一 builtin 是 vm2，沙箱可 require('vm2') 构造内层 NodeVM 直通 child_process RCE）；且守卫用严格 === true 比较 nesting、未要求 requireOpts 为对象——truthy 非 true 的 nesting（1/'yes'/{}）与 truthy 非对象 require（true/1/函数，解构后全 undefined）都可绕过。fix 86ab819 改为结构守卫 nesting && hasRealRequireConfig（requireOpts 必须是非 null 对象或 Resolver）。

blocked106.flaw_semantics: Per shard mapping (sink pkix/.../est/HttpAuth.java): the digest-algorithm name in the EST Digest auth WWW-Authenticate header is server-supplied; HttpAuth.lookupDigest() passes it to DefaultDigestAlgorithmIdentifierFinder.find(String) which for an unrecognized name returns null (pre-fix) -> caller turns null into IOException 'auth digest algorithm unknown'. partial_wave.bug_semantics: Out-of-bounds read of one byte in PrintStringInfo() when identify displays a non-printable profile: the hex-dump row loop runs j from 1 to MagickMin(length-i,CharsPerLine) and reads *(p+j), so on the last row (when length % CharsPerLine == 0) it dereferences datum[length], one byte past the profile buffer, and prints it (CWE-125).
partial_wave.flaw_origin: The hex-dump loop in PrintStringInfo was written with row-internal index j starting at 1 instead of 0 while reading *(p+j), so each row's final byte is the next row's first and the last row reads datum[length]; the 2026 fix starts j at 0 and indexes p[i+j].
partial_wave.evidence: GHSA-hwf3-r46v-5ggx (2026-07, Magick.NET, fixed 14.15.0): 'When a profile is displayed with the identify command and the value is not printable a single byte at the end of the profile can be printed.' Fix 4079949bae (2026-06-05, Cristy) rewrites PrintStringInfo (MagickCore/string.c:1496) so the hex loop is 'for (j = 0; j < MagickMin(length-i, CharsPerLine); j++) ... p[i+j]', eliminating the off-by-one. git log -G 'j <= MagickMin' shows the flawed j=1..MagickMin(...,0x14) loop with *(p+j) already in 4c08aed51 (2011-07-01, cristy, human) where PrintStringInfo's hex dump was written; 7c6601dae (2018-04-26, Cristy) only resized the row width. No AI markers.
partial_wave.reasoning: The one-byte OOB print loop was written by human maintainer cristy in 2011. NOT_AI.

blocked106.flaw_semantics: Heap-based buffer overflow in LightPcapNg parser parse_by_block_type(): in the Enhanced Packet Block path, captured_packet_length is read from the file and used both for the calloc size (PADD32 into actual_len) and as the memcpy length (memcpy(epb->packet_data, local_data, captured_packet_length)) without bounding against remaining block/file data, so a crafted pcapng with captured_packet_length larger than available input overflows the heap. Same unbounded pattern exists in the Simple Packet Block path (actual_len from block_total_length, line ~193).

partial_wave.bug_semantics: Merge node SQL query mode: user-supplied SQL query is executed via alasql (db.exec(query)) with no restriction on code-execution constructs; alasql supports CREATE FUNCTION, REQUIRE/yy.Require, utils.require and JavaScript engine so an authenticated user with workflow create/edit permissions can execute arbitrary code and write arbitrary files on the n8n server. Later hardening only blocked file FROM/INTO/engine handlers (79f1cca9af0, 9ce3ac092cf, 70c573c8822) but left code-exec vectors open until the final fix froze alasql.fn/yy and disabled utils.require/REQUIRE/yy.JavaScript.

partial_wave.bug_semantics: Use-after-free (CWE-416) in the MSL decoder: ReadMSLImage/ProcessMSLScript parse the script from the input blob held by the MSL image (msl_image->blob) via a libxml2 push parser, but the MSL coder had the default CoderBlobSupportFlag so the caller could hand it a live in-memory blob whose lifetime is not tied to the parser; script-triggered image list operations can free the blob memory while the SAX parser is still consuming it, yielding a use-after-free (crash reported via Magick.NET reading MSL from byte arrays).
partial_wave.flaw_origin: The MSL coder was written in the original import parsing the script straight from the blob stream with no temp-file indirection; the 2026 fix clears CoderBlobSupportFlag (flags^=) so GetMagickBlobSupport() returns false and blob inputs are spooled to a stable temporary file before parsing, decoupling blob lifetime from the XML parser.
partial_wave.evidence: GHSA-5r4x-w6p5-222q / CVE-2026-46523 (2026-05, Magick.NET, fixed 14.13.1): use-after-free in MSL decoder. Fix 4d92249c84 (2026-05-13, Cristy, message = advisory URL) is a one-liner in RegisterMSLImage: entry->flags^=CoderBlobSupportFlag (coders/msl.c:7588); since AcquireMagickInfo defaults flags to CoderAdjoinFlag | CoderBlobSupportFlag (MagickCore/magick.c:188) the XOR removes blob support, and GetMagickBlobSupport()/OpenBlob then route blob inputs through a temp file instead of parsing from live blob memory (MagickCore/blob.c:835, 2543). The MSL coder has parsed script chunks from the blob via xmlParseChunk since the repository root commit 3ed852eea (2009-09-05, cristy, initial import, human; coders/msl.c:7527-7540 at root). No AI markers.
partial_wave.reasoning: The blob-lifetime hazard in the MSL coder was written by human maintainer cristy in the original 2009 import. NOT_AI.

partial_wave.bug_semantics: In DuplexFramingMiddleware, SingletonFramingMiddleware, and RawStream, the framing handshake read loops invoked PipeReader.ReadAsync without checking readResult.IsCompleted or passing a cancellation token. When a client closed the connection after sending only the preamble, subsequent ReadAsync calls returned synchronously with an empty buffer and IsCompleted=true; because buffer.Length == 0, the inner loop was skipped and the outer loop spun in a 100% CPU infinite loop ignoring handshake timeouts.
partial_wave.flaw_origin: The framing handshake ReadAsync loop lacking IsCompleted / premature EOF checks was written by Matt Connew in 4df75ac7 ('Initial port of NetTcp' / early CoreWCF, 2019-06-03) and 349aad21 (2021-02-02).
partial_wave.evidence: Fix commit 03ddbce (2026-04-30) treats IsCompleted && Buffer.IsEmpty as premature EOF and passes ChannelInitializationCancellationToken. Git blame traces the handshake read loop to human commits 4df75ac7 (Matt Connew, 2019-06-03) and 349aad21 (Matt Connew, 2021-02-02), with no AI markers in the introducer lineage.
partial_wave.reasoning: The framing handshake infinite loop bug was written by CoreWCF maintainer Matt Connew in early 2019-2021 human code. All introducers are human.

partial_wave.bug_semantics: HTTP request smuggling via HTTP/1.0 and Transfer-Encoding misparsing: (1) HTTP/1.0 request bodies without Content-Length were treated as close-delimited (init_http10), but RFC 9112 says requests are never close-delimited; (2) Transfer-Encoding detection was an exact-match of the whole header value against 'chunked', so comma-separated/multiple TE headers (e.g. 'identity, chunked') or non-chunked TE were mis-framed; (3) non-chunked final Transfer-Encoding was accepted - together allowing desync of request framing vs backends and request smuggling past proxy ACLs/WAF

partial_wave.evidence: advisory GHSA-hj7x-879w-vrp7 / RUSTSEC-2026-0034, fixed in 0.8.0 by three commits (ledger fix_sha faac65b0c2a0 is only the 0.8.0 CHANGELOG commit): 7f7166d62 Fei Deng 2026-01-27 'transfer-encoding parsing robustness' (is_chunked_encoding_from_headers parses last comma-separated token across all TE headers), 40c3c1e9a Edward Wang 2026-01-30 'Avoid close delimit mode on http/1.0 req' (requests without CL/TE end after header section; close-delimited responses disable reuse), 87e2e2fb3 Edward Wang 2026-02-11 'Reject non-chunked transfer-encoding' (400 on HTTP/1.0 TE or non-chunked final TE). squash_audit.bug_semantics: 浏览器工具的 Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) 直连 WebSocket 支持（createTargetViaCdp）：当 cdpUrl 为 ws:// 或 wss:// 时，直接建立 WebSocket 连接并跳过 /json/version 探测流程，但遗漏了对该 WebSocket 端点进行 SSRF 安全策略校验（assertCdpEndpointAllowed）；攻击者可利用 direct websocket URL（如 ws://169.254.169.254:9222/...）绕过 SSRF 防护探测/连接内网与云元数据服务（GHSA-F7FH-QG34-X2XH / #60469）。

squash_audit.evidence: candidate 75602014dbc adds direct WebSocket branch in src/browser/cdp.ts:109-113 ('if (isWebSocketUrl(opts.cdpUrl)) { wsUrl = opts.cdpUrl; }') without SSRF check; fix bc356cc8 adds 'await assertCdpEndpointAllowed(opts.cdpUrl, opts.ssrfPolicy);' to that branch; candidate is a single-parent feature commit carrying Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6.

blocked106.flaw_semantics: Authenticated RCE (CWE-94/78) in the cron scheduler: job type 'function' takes the DB-stored methodename and passes it directly to call_user_func_array($this->methodename, $params_arr) with no allowlist or blacklist; params are split on commas and passed unfiltered. methodename is accepted via GETPOST('methodename','aZ09') so 'system' passes, and any installed module lib (e.g. zapier.lib.php) passes the dol_include_once existence check, making the function-call primitive usable for arbitrary PHP/OS calls. blocked106.flaw_semantics: GitLab EE authenticated DoS (CWE-770): a user with developer access uploads a crafted flow-style YAML dashboard config to .gitlab/analytics/dashboards/<slug>/<slug>.yaml in the group's dashboard-configuration project, then repeatedly fires the GraphQL operation getAllCustomizableDashboards (Analytics::Dashboards::Dashboard.for -> customized_dashboards). Each request parses the attacker-controlled YAML with plain YAML.safe_load with no size/depth/complexity limits, so a deeply-nested flow-style payload causes uncontrolled CPU/memory consumption and the instance becomes unavailable at ~1 RPS.

blocked106.flaw_semantics: Improper access control (CWE-284/200) in share views: ShareService.getViewRecords() passes the client-supplied `projection` query parameter straight through to recordService.getRecords() (`projection: query?.projection ?? filteredFields.map(f => f.id)`).
